trial_court: High Court of Himachal Pradesh, Shimla (CrMMO No. 910 of 2024)
case_name: Divyanshu Awasthi and Ors. v. State of Himachal Pradesh and Anr.

parties.respondent_defendant: State of Himachal Pradesh and respondent No.2

facts_of_case: Petitioner's wife alleged maltreatment due to less dowry, harassment, and was compelled to leave her matrimonial house. Parties entered into compromise and filed petition under Section 13(B) of the Hindu Marriage Act for dissolution of marriage by mutual consent.

legal_principles.principle: Power under S. 482 CrPC is not to be exercised in cases which involve heinous and serious offences.
legal_principles.held: The power conferred under Section 482 of the Code is to be distinguished from the power which lies in the Court to compound the offences under Section 320 of the Code.
cited_cases: Narinder Singh and others versus State of Punjab and another, (2014)6 SCC 466
use_in: case type: murder or serious offence cases
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to guide courts in exercising discretion under S. 482 CrPC

legal_principles.principle: The power to quash criminal proceedings under S. 482 of the Code is to be exercised sparingly and with great caution.
legal_principles.held: No doubt, under Section 482 of the Code, the High Court has inherent power to quash criminal proceedings even in those cases which are not compoundable and where the parties have settled the matter between themselves; however, this power is to be exercised sparingly and with great caution.
cited_cases: Narinder Singh and others versus State of Punjab and another, (2014)6 SCC 466
use_in: case type: criminal proceedings quashing cases
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to guide courts in exercising discretion under S. 482 CrPC

outcome.final_order: FIR No. 156/22, dated 17.9.2022, under Sections 498-A, 506 and 34 of IPC, registered with Police Station Joginder Nagar, District Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, was quashed.
